critique:
the policy prompt for subgoal
  Failures occurred when the hand was empty and the policy had to select the next cube for goals requesting three blue and two green, two red, three red, or one blue and two green cubes. Completed releases were correctly reflected in the deposit counters, but the policy selected a different visible cube or color through the smallest-y fallback or an insufficiently distinguished nearby-layout preference. The counters were correct; these are SUFFICIENCY failures in target selection, not PREDICTABILITY failures in memory updates. Preserve the existing memory fields, deposit recognition, quota checks, held-cube-to-B rule, and completion-to-C rule. Extend the scene-conditioned preferences with the following complete goal-and-layout rules, evaluated using updated counters before the fallback. For three blue and two green with the bin near [112, 161], finish blue first: select blue near [66, 141], [81, 71], and [94, 131] when blue_deposited is respectively zero, one, and two; after three blue deposits select green near [78, 109] and [72, 172] when green_deposited is respectively zero and one. This arrangement also has persistent blue candidates near [60, 165] and [84, 88], and green candidates near [58, 128], [96, 188], and [107, 100]; use the visible remaining arrangement to distinguish it from the existing blue-first layout with bin near [101, 141], rather than mapping that layout's green preference to the cube near [96, 188]. For two red with bin near [95, 162], select red near [53, 80] when red_deposited is zero and near [77, 139] when it is one. At the latter stage, other visible red candidates can include [74, 161], [100, 66], and [119, 153]; the smaller y of [74, 161] must not override the preference. For three red with bin near [109, 112], select red near [113, 142], [70, 82], and [95, 158] when red_deposited is respectively zero, one, and two. At two deposits, remaining candidates near [79, 88], [85, 117], and [106, 155] distinguish this arrangement and must not displace the preferred [95, 158] cube. For one blue and two green with bin near [109, 100], finish green first: select green near [108, 152] and [75, 88] when green_deposited is respectively zero and one, then select blue near [117, 71] once green_deposited is two and blue_deposited is zero. Other visible candidates, including green near [68, 160] and [98, 77] and blue near [54, 173] and [63, 75], do not override these choices. These are conditional selection rules, not a stored action sequence: apply them only with an empty hand and an outstanding quota, matching the goal, bin, and currently observable remaining cube arrangement together. Initial scenes may reveal only the first target; do not require later-revealed cubes or already deposited cubes to be visible. Use approximate reference positions to identify objects and output a point within the selected cube at its current observed position, in [y, x] order. Retain the existing preferences for other layouts and the fallback for genuinely unmatched layouts or unavailable preferred candidates; no existing rule needs wholesale removal.
